picks.what: Bird’s-eye view, engraving in Braun and Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum, vol. 3 (colored copy of the 1645 French edition)
picks.why: colored bird’s-eye view of the walled city with its churches and the old castle drawn; already cut to the plate (same scan as #6)

picks.what: The Grand Place, photochrom print (Library of Congress)
picks.why: color; the main square with the Goddess column and the belfry of the Grand’Garde; frame and caption cut
dated 8 July 1935; whole city with Vauban’s star-shaped citadel; dark wing shadow at the bottom cut

picks.what: View over the city center, photograph
picks.why: high view toward the old town with the Chamber of Commerce belfry; modern buildings in front; best of a weak modern set

gaps: P0: no view (#1 is a portrait woodcut). P2: no usable view. P3: no candidates (only portraits).
notes: P2: Van der Meulen’s wide view of Lille with the king’s army before the town in 1667 (#13 full print, #12 right half) is a strong view but an event scene whose engraving date is unknown (records give only 1632–90 or 1654–1711), so left out; worth adding if the print can be dated. Merian’s ‘Lille Rysselia’ (#10) is a plan of uncertain edition. #16–17 are Bergen, Norway (photochrom of Lille Lungegårdsvann lake), not Lille. #7–8 are Rhodes and Famagusta.
